title: Scope-tagged service credential playbook and rotation policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a practical engineering playbook, APIs, and migration plan for scope-tagged service credentials (per-scope API keys), standardized naming, enforced expiry/rotation, and audit logging. This covers runtime changes (introspection, revocation), control plane UX, and migration from existing long-lived keys to scoped tokens tied into RBAC v2 and SSO groups.
background: Existing API keys are long-lived, inconsistently named, and lack per-scope granularity which increases blast radius and complicates audits. This ticket defines how to issue, rotate, audit, and revoke scoped credentials while integrating with RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML mappings.
goals: Define a machine-parseable, human-friendly naming convention for keys
Implement per-scope (least-privilege) service credentials with explicit expiration
Add a token introspection and revocation API and integrate with audit logging
Design a safe rolling rotation strategy with shadow-keys for minimal downtime
Provide migration tooling and console UX for discovery and upgrading existing keys
out_of_scope: Full replacement of OAuth flows for end-user auth
Hard-enforcing token use at every microservice boundary (left for service teams)
design_summary: 1) Introduce 'scope' as a first-class attribute on credentials: scopes map to RBAC v2 permissions or named capability bundles (e.g., 'models:infer:read', 'admin:billing'). 2) Enforce TTLs at issuance; default TTLs by scope sensitivity (ephemeral 1h for admin-console tokens, 90d for service-to-service limited-scope tokens). 3) Naming: svc-{team}-{env}-{purpose}-{YYYYMMDD}-{shortid} with metadata tags. 4) Control plane: issue, list (partial key display), rotate (create shadow, switch, revoke), revoke endpoints. 5) Runtime: lightweight introspection endpoint with cached policy result and transparent audit events. 6) Audit logs: ensure token_id, issuer_id, subject_id, scope_list, action, ip, user_agent, region, request_id are recorded for every issuance/use/revocation.
detailed_decisions: Use bearer tokens (HMAC-based signed tokens) for immediate rollout; evaluate migrating to mTLS or JWT with KMS-signed claims in later phases
Short-lived tokens are preferred; provide managed refresh tokens only for long-lived service workflows with strict scope and rotation windows
Naming must be parseable; include date and shortid for uniqueness to make forensic timelines easier
Expose only last 4 chars of token in the console; full secret shown once at creation and never after
Introspection endpoint will return cached policy evaluation for 60s to reduce latency cost for high-throughput inferences
api_contracts: POST /v1/credentials - body: {subject_id, scopes[], ttl, tags[]} returns credential_id and one-time secret
GET /v1/credentials/{id} - metadata (no secret) including scopes, created_at, expires_at, name, tags
POST /v1/credentials/{id}/rotate - creates shadow credential, returns transition token id
POST /v1/introspect - body: {token} returns {active, credential_id, scopes[], subject_id, expires_at, policy_hash}
audit_log_schema: Each event must include: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, token_id, action (issue|use|introspect|rotate|revoke), scopes, resource, request_id, ip, user_agent, region, outcome, reason. Logs written to immutable append-only store with replication to long-term analytics and SIEM (90d hot, 2y cold).
rotation_policy: Default rotation rules: ephemeral scopes (session-like) TTL <= 1h and auto-delete; low-sensitivity service scopes TTL 90d, require rotation reminder at 7d before expiry; high-sensitivity/admin scopes TTL 30d with enforced automated rotation every 30d; emergency rotation can be triggered via revoke all tokens for subject_id or per-token revoke. Shadow-rotation flow: create new token, allow dual acceptance window (default 10m), switch route, then revoke old token.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Inventory and tagging - run a discovery job to map existing keys to owners/team and usage patterns. Phase 2: Optional auto-conversion for low-use keys: issue scoped token and mark old token deprecated with expiration. Phase 3: Enforced migration - disable issuance of new unconstrained tokens and require scoped tokens in new projects. Phase 4: Clean-up - revoke all pre-migration long-lived keys after 90d deprecation window.
console_changes: Credential creation UX will require selecting scopes from a curated RBAC-capability list, TTL selector with recommended defaults, naming override prefilled per team, and a preflight risk score. Listing will show last 4 chars of secret, scope badges, created/expires timestamps, and a 'rotate' and 'revoke' action on each row.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: tokens_by_scope, tokens_nearing_expiry, tokens_revoked_by_user, failed_introspections_by_region. Alerts: >5% failed introspections in 5m, sudden surge in revocations, creation of admin-scope tokens outside exempted teams. Integrate with PagerDuty runbooks for emergency revocation.
acceptance_criteria: APIs implemented and documented (issue/list/rotate/revoke/introspect) with tests
Console flows for create/list/rotate/revoke staged behind feature flag
Audit logs validate presence of token_id and action for every issuance/use/revoke
Migration discovery job runs and produces owner mapping for >95% of active keys
Automated rotation and revoke flows tested in staging with canary traffic and zero-production downtime
test_plan: Unit tests for API contract, integration tests for introspection latency under load, chaos test where old token revoked during active inference load, security fuzz tests to ensure no secret leakage in logs, end-to-end migration dry-run against sample org.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood org rollout, 2) Beta with 3 customer orgs (opt-in), 3) Gradual default enablement for new organizations, 4) Forced migration window announced 60d before enforcement. Each stage gated by security review and SLO for introspection latency (<2ms median) and no increase in inference error rates.
rollback_plan: If introspection errors or unexpected user impact seen, disable enforcement flag and revert routing to accept both scoped and legacy tokens while investigating root cause. Use audit logs to identify failing token patterns.
open_questions: Should refresh tokens be allowed for service-to-service flows and under what strict controls?
Do we want machine-readable scope bundles (predefined) or allow freeform scopes with validation?
What is the optimal dual-acceptance window for shadow rotation in very high-throughput inference endpoints?
